newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BIG BALTIC SHIPYARD STAKE SOLD AT BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: BIG BALTIC SHIPYARD STAKE SOLD AT BOURSE.

text.p: Lithuania's stock exchange said on Monday that 16.27 percent of the shares of Baltic Shipyard were sold in an auction at the bourse.
The stock exchange would not say who bought the shares, which turned over 11.4 million litas at 10.10 litas a share, but that the Vilfima brokerage was involved.
"There were only two bids," said Saulius Merkys, a broker with Vilfima.
Baltic Shipyard shares traded at 7.92 litas on the central market, turning over about 55,000 litas.
Rimas Jakuchionis, director of state-owned brokerage Prohema, which executed the deal, told Reuters the initial price in the auction was ten litas.
"The share portfolio of 1.126 million ordinary shares was sold," Jakuchionis said.
He declined to say who bought the shares but said the buyer had to release the information in five days.
Baltic Shipyard had been included on a list of 14 key state enterprises to be sold by open international bidding until Denmark's Odense shipyard bought over 40 percent of the company in March.
The state owned 32 percent of Baltic Shipyard's 34.6 million litas share capital.
The state's stake was cut by half when it did not use its priority right to buy into the new share issue after shareholders decided to double its share capital earlier this year.
The European affairs ministry said earlier that Odense was offering to buy the government's stake at above the market price.
